topics.label: Introduction to complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides introductory framing for the lecture and sets expectations regarding complement nomenclature.

topics.label: Fundamentals of complement and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the complement system, explain its naming conventions, and describe the central role of C3 in activation.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three recognition pathways that converge to drive complement activation past its trigger threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated complement destroys pathogens through opsonization, recruitment of inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the distinct clinical presentations and disease phenotypes that result from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens evade complement attack and how evasion molecules are repurposed in medical and laboratory applications.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
